[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll aim for an hour, we've got a fairly packed agenda. Lucas is gonna lead the profiling bits. ravi, could you quickly confirm the failing symptoms one more time?
[00:14] Ravi Menon: yeah sure, so the core issue is when we enable CUDA graph replay on our - on prem clusters, after a few thousand requests we start to see either p99 jump by like two to three x or in rare cases token corruption on outputs, like a single token that becomes a repeated character. it's quite subtle but repros in our load test.
[00:37] Lucas Patel: ok got it. and the stack there is TensorRT-LLM pipelines? or are you using the open-source runtime, like vLLM, as a fallback?
[00:46] Sofia Alvarez: we run a mixed stack. production uses TRT-LLM for the low-latency paths, but in dev we have vllm-based endpoints for experiments. the failing behavior is seen on TRT more often.
[01:02] Mark Johnson: also want to call out that we're pinned to a NUMA-aware node layout with nvlink cross connects, and our KMS is internal, so any repro we share needs to be sanitized.
[01:15] Maya Chen: understood. Lucas, quick plan — we should determine whether it's a kernel selection mismatch under replay vs non-replay, or a KV cache eviction race coupled with quantized kernels returning slightly off-values that cascade. i know you've been running a fuzz harness, right?
[01:31] Lucas Patel: yeah, i built a small quant-fuzz runner that flips quantization scales and runs many short sequences to try and catch divergence. what we've noticed on Redwood Dedicated runs is that when cuda graph replay is enabled, the kernel fusion path will sometimes choose a fused matmul+softmax variant that later does a different kernel on replay, there's a small path id mismatch. which is surprising cause cuda graph should serialize the exact calls.
[02:00] Ravi Menon: hmm, that aligns with what we see — the first hour is fine then it diverges. do you think it's nondeterminism in kernel selection, or could it be memory aliasing in the replay buffer?
[02:14] Lucas Patel: could be both. we've seen a case where persistent KV cache prefetch sets a buffer as reusable, and on replay the pointer offsets differ due to allocator reuse, so the graph replays correct sequence of ops but with different underlying addresses which some kernels (especially fused ones) assume for in-place transforms.
[02:36] Sofia Alvarez: that's worrying. on our side we also run a custom allocator around the HBM to try and reduce NUMA friction. could that interact?
[02:44] Lucas Patel: yes, custom allocators increase the chance of different base pointers across runs. we recommend using a deterministic arena allocator for replay tests. for on-prem, we can run an isolated job that pins the arena and disables ASLR, but i know that's heavy handed.
[03:01] Mark Johnson: quick question — when you say "fused matmul+softmax variant" is that a TRT-specific kernel? or something coming from JIT in vllm?
[03:10] Lucas Patel: primarily TRT fuse variants. vLLM tends to be more modular for ops, but TRT will pick a fused kernel if it meets heuristics. fusion heuristics can change depending on workspace memory availability and sequence length, so under different batch distributions you may get a different kernel picked.
[03:29] Maya Chen: and quantization makes small numeric differences that may push kernel heuristics across a threshold, no?
[03:35] Lucas Patel: exactly. a per-channel scale change can alter activation sparsity leading TRT to prefer a fused kernel that assumes certain memory layout for performance. if that kernel is later replayed with different offsets, you get havoc.
[03:51] Ravi Menon: in our perf traces we saw kernel IDs flip between replays, and sometimes a memcpy op inserted that shouldn't be there.
[03:59] Lucas Patel: memcpy insertion often points to staging buffers getting allocated to satisfy alignment. That's a good clue.
[04:07] Maya Chen: ok let's drill into the repro you shared. ravi, you uploaded a replay tarball and a flamegraph to the bench sheet — can you point us to the exact run?
[04:17] Ravi Menon: yes in the sheet there's a tab labeled "failing-replay-0916"; the S3 path in the notes points to a capture folder. the capture shows a delta at 12:13:22 where p99 went from 72ms to 240ms over 30 minutes.
[04:35] Lucas Patel: i'll pull that now. (brief pause) ok i see the trace, and there's a sequence where the NVTX ranges show graph capture start/stop, then later a capture with identical op counts but different kernel names. interesting.
[04:55] Sofia Alvarez: we also have a hunch that our KV cache prefetch window (we're prefetching 8 steps) may be evicting older entries under high concurrency, leading to slightly different key layout.
[05:08] Lucas Patel: prefetch=8 is on the higher side. that may increase pressure on allocator and push fusion heuristics. For a sensitive replay run, recommend prefetch=2 or disabled, and see if the p99 stabilizes.
[05:21] Mark Johnson: does Redwood Optimize have a tunable rule here? like auto suggest prefetch downscaling?
[05:28] Maya Chen: yes, Optimize can suggest batching and prefetch settings per workload. we can run a quick eval to show the cost/latency tradeoff, but given this is nondeterministic, first step is repro and deterministic capture.
[05:41] Ravi Menon: about quantization — we use 4-bit asymmetric per-channel for most models. could the quantization kernels themselves be nondet under different cuda graph capture timing?
[05:54] Lucas Patel: quant kernels are usually deterministic, but in fused kernels you can have reduction ops that rely on parallel accumulation order which may be non-associative for low-bit arith. small order differences can produce tiny numeric deltas that later cause different branch choices.
[06:10] Maya Chen: so actionably: we need a minimal repro that toggles three variables — cuda_graph on/off, prefetch window, and quantization profile — and then we run a pairwise matrix to isolate which combo triggers it.
[06:23] Lucas Patel: agreed. i'll prepare a harness that runs the customer's model with randomized seeds but fixed allocator for replay, runs 2k short sequences and dumps kernel IDs per iteration. that should show whether kernel selection flips correlate with p99.
[06:37] Ravi Menon: we'll sanitize and get you the failing capture. also want to try running the same harness on one of Redwood's Dedicated nodes to see if it's infra related.
[06:46] Maya Chen: good, we'll queue a dedicated slot in us-west-2 for that run. Lucas, can you also run the quant-fuzz runner you mentioned earlier and attach the logs?
[06:54] Lucas Patel: yes, i'll attach the zip to the ticket. also FYI i noticed in internal testing that when cuda graphs are used with persistent KV cache, enabling "graph rebind" in TRT helps in some cases, it forces kernel bind semantics. but it can increase latency slightly.
[07:10] Sofia Alvarez: what's "graph rebind"? is that an option we can toggle without code changes?
[07:15] Lucas Patel: depends on TRT version; it's a flag to recreate the graph when certain memory layouts change instead of assuming pointer stability. in Redwood Dedicated we can enable it at runtime for the test.
[07:26] Mark Johnson: tradeoff accepted if it buys determinism for canary tests.
[07:31] Maya Chen: let's capture decisions for the pilot: run matrix with graph rebind on/off, prefetch 2 vs 8, quant 4-bit baseline vs fallback 8-bit, and replay vs no replay. that'll be 2x2x2x2 = 16 runs; do we all agree?
[07:47] Ravi Menon: yes that's reasonable.
[07:50] Lucas Patel: i recommend we also capture raw allocator traces and include the device pointer base addresses in the logs so we can confirm pointer drift.
[07:59] Sofia Alvarez: we can enable verbose allocator tracing on our cluster for the failing window.
[08:03] Maya Chen: ok next, timing and owners — maya will schedule Redwood Dedicated slot, lucas will deliver harness and run initial quant-fuzz, ravi will fetch and sanitize trace and upload. we want first bench results by 2026-09-29.
[08:19] Mark Johnson: one more ask — we need an explanation doc for our security team about how Redwood handles replay artifacts and keys, basically to satisfy our compliance check. can you provide that?
[08:30] Maya Chen: yes we'll share the security whitepaper and a redacted replay guide. i'll add it to the ticket.
[08:36] Lucas Patel: also i'll note known TRT versions where graph rebind is available; in some older TRT builds the option isn't present and the workaround is to set a small padding on allocations.
[08:47] Ravi Menon: ok thanks, this was helpful. any final questions?
[08:52] Maya Chen: none from us. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the ticket and schedule the bench run.
